newsitem.title: USA: U.S. steel producers ask Congress to stop dumping.
newsitem.headline: U.S. steel producers ask Congress to stop dumping.

text.p: U.S. steel mills urged Congress on Thursday to strictly enforce trade laws and prevent dumping by China, the Commonwealth of Independent States and other nations.

"Of immediate concern to our members is the surge of unfairly traded steel products flooding the entire NAFTA region from 'nonmarket economies' such as the CIS countries and the People's Republic of China," said C.H. Barnette, who is chairman of Bethlehem Steel Corp and head of the American Iron and Steel Institute.

Barnette, who spoke to the Congressional and Senate Steel Caucuses, also said steel producers were concerned about the rising value of the U.S. dollar against the yen and the mark. "Experience shows that the United States must stringently monitor foreign governments' policies and actions to ensure that they do not manipulate their currency's exchange rate."
Steel producers also said they opposed more stringent clean air standards until there was scientific evidence about health benefits.

"The Environmental Protection Agency's current proposals for revised air quality standards are based upon ambiguous and unclear science and could increase compliance burdens on the industry by more than $1 billion annually," said Robert Cardy, a spokesman for Specialty Steel Industry of North America.
